claim.why_it_matters: Printed page 906 (A-76) ends with rule (3) of the WHEN-COMPILED Returned Values and carries no amendment heading. The markdown adds a top-level heading '# AMENDMENT 2: CORRECTION AMENDMENT (ANSI X3.23b-1993)' after the A-76 folio, inside the Page 906 slice, and does not mark it as an editorial note. The part divider belongs before the amendment's cover (page 907), and its wording is not printed anywhere on page 906. Nothing normative is lost, but the page slice for 906 holds text the page does not print, and the part boundary falls inside the wrong page.

verdict.reasoning: The 300 dpi render of page 906 (A-76) shows the WHEN-COMPILED table row 20-21 and rules (2) and (3), then the A-76 folio. The markdown slice reproduces all of that text verbatim. The only extra line is '# AMENDMENT 2: CORRECTION AMENDMENT (ANSI X3.23b-1993)', a document part divider the transcriber inserted at the boundary between Amendment 1 and Amendment 2. It sits directly before the '## Page 907' marker, so it falls at the page boundary. It changes no text that page 906 prints, and page 907's slice still carries the amendment's printed cover (ANSI INCITS 23b-1993 ... Correction Amendment for COBOL). The difference is navigation scaffolding at a page break, not a content discrepancy, and it changes no meaning. A slice-boundary tool could attribute the line to page 906, but that is a formatting and placement matter the verification rules exclude.
